schema_lineage.schema_id: TEMPLATE_MQ_Gap_Schema — replace with your schema ID (e.g., MyMarket_MQ_Gap_Schema)
schema_lineage.parent_schema: TEMPLATE — filename of the corresponding capability schema this supplements (e.g., My_Market_Capability_Schema.json)
related_schemas: TEMPLATE — list related capability or pricing schema filenames, or remove this array
schema_lineage.purpose: TEMPLATE — one sentence: 'Supplemental MQ evaluation criteria NOT addressed by the [MARKET NAME] capability schema. Scored independently, then combined via mq_scoring_mode to produce final Magic Quadrant positions for the [MARKET NAME] market.'

mq_gap_schema_template_v1.0.intent: TEMPLATE — 2-3 sentences: What does this schema evaluate? Which 7 MQ criteria gaps does it cover? How do these scores combine with capability scores? Example: 'Evaluate [MARKET NAME] vendors against the 7 Magic Quadrant criteria gaps: Financial Viability, Sales Execution, Market Responsiveness, Marketing Execution, Customer Experience Quality, Market Understanding & Vision, and Vertical & Geographic Strategy. These supplement the [MARKET NAME] technical capability assessment to complete the full MQ evaluation framework. Combined scores produce the Ability to Execute and Completeness of Vision axis positions used in Magic Quadrant placement.'

metadata.framework_alignment: TEMPLATE — cite the specific Gartner MQ methodology document this schema aligns to (e.g., 'Gartner Magic Quadrant Evaluation Framework — G00802987 (2 July 2025); Gartner Market Guide for [MARKET NAME]'). The document ID ensures the schema stays tied to a specific methodology version.
metadata.applies_to: TEMPLATE — short market name (e.g., CNAPP, MDR, OffSec, PreCyber). This value appears in UI labels.

capability_scoring_scale.meaning_of_zero: No Evidence — No public data or documentation found
capability_scoring_scale._note: MQ Gap schemas use a slightly different scoring vocabulary than capability schemas — emphasizing evidence breadth and business indicators rather than technical depth. The 0-5 scale is shared across all schemas in this platform. Do not modify scale values.

scoring_logic.0: No Evidence — no public data, documentation, or third-party references available.
scoring_logic.1: Minimal — vague or unsubstantiated claims only; no verifiable evidence.
scoring_logic.2: Basic — some evidence found but significant gaps remain; limited depth.
scoring_logic.3: Demonstrated — clear evidence of capability with moderate depth across multiple sources.
scoring_logic.4: Strong — well-documented with multiple proof points from credible sources.
scoring_logic.5: Market-Leading — best-in-class with extensive evidence and third-party validation.

source_policy._note: MQ Gap schemas require different evidence sources than capability schemas — financial, business, and market-execution evidence rather than technical documentation. The tiering below reflects this. Adjust examples to match the specific market.

valid_sources._note: Tier 1 sources are authoritative and carry full weight. Required for scores of 4+.

examples: TEMPLATE — name the specific Gartner MQ or Market Guide for this market
Forrester Wave for the relevant market category
IDC MarketScape for the relevant market category

valid_sources._note: Tier 2 sources are valid supporting evidence. Sufficient for scores up to 3-4 when multiple Tier 2 sources agree.
examples: TEMPLATE — Gartner Peer Insights category for this market

valid_sources._note: Tier 3 sources alone cannot justify scores above 2. Use only as corroborating signals.
examples: Job postings as proxy for investment

coverage_grade._note: Same grading scale as capability schemas. Adjust thresholds to match your total sub-pillar count across all 7 MQ Gap pillars.

mq_axis_mapping._note: This block maps pillar codes to the two MQ axes. The standard 7 pillars (VIA, SLE, MKR, MKE, CXQ, MKU, VIG) map to axes as shown below. SLE and MKE contribute to BOTH axes per Gartner MQ methodology. Adjust the lists if your schema uses different pillar codes or a different axis weighting model.
mq_axis_mapping.note: SLE (Sales Execution) and MKE (Marketing Execution) contribute to BOTH axes per Gartner MQ methodology — sales strategy feeds Completeness of Vision while execution feeds Ability to Execute.

pillars._note: The 7 pillars below are the standard Gartner MQ Gap criteria used across all MQ Gap schemas in this platform. Keep the pillar codes (VIA, SLE, MKR, MKE, CXQ, MKU, VIG) consistent — the platform uses them to map to MQ axes. Customize the focus descriptions, mq_criterion references, and evidence_signals to match your specific market. The mq_criterion codes (ATE-N, COV-N) reference the Gartner MQ evaluation framework document cited in metadata.framework_alignment above.

VIA.name: Financial Viability & Stability
VIA.focus: TEMPLATE — overall financial health of the vendor in this specific market, business unit investment level, and likelihood of continued product development and support. Maps to MQ criterion ATE-2 (Overall Viability). For pure-play vendors, assess startup runway and funding. For platform vendors, assess how strategically important this market is within the broader portfolio.
evidence_signals: TEMPLATE — SEC filings or annual reports showing revenue in this market segment
TEMPLATE — Funding announcements or valuation milestones specific to this market
TEMPLATE — Analyst estimates of market share in this segment
TEMPLATE — Headcount growth in this market as a proxy for investment

SLE.name: Sales Execution & Channel
SLE.focus: TEMPLATE — presales depth, direct sales team quality, channel strategy (MSSP, SI, reseller), and marketplace reach relevant to this specific market. Maps to MQ criteria ATE-3 (Sales Execution) and COV-3 (Sales Strategy). Consider which channels are most relevant to buyers in this market — enterprise direct, SMB PLG, channel-heavy, or hyperscaler co-sell.
evidence_signals: TEMPLATE — Marketplace listings relevant to this market (e.g., AWS, Azure, GCP for cloud markets; MSSP partner programs for services markets)
TEMPLATE — Channel partner program documentation and named partners
TEMPLATE — Self-service trial or POV program availability
TEMPLATE — Sales team geographic coverage (office locations, job postings)

MKR.name: Market Responsiveness & Track Record
MKR.focus: TEMPLATE — ability to respond to market shifts specific to this segment. What are the key market trends vendors must respond to? What does a fast responder look like vs. a laggard? Maps to MQ criterion ATE-4. Example for MDR: vendors responding to AI-assisted triage and autonomous detection. Example for CNAPP: vendors responding to AI-SPM, runtime convergence, and agentless adoption.
evidence_signals: TEMPLATE — Release notes and changelogs showing response to market trends in this segment
TEMPLATE — Major capability additions responding to market evolution over the last 12-24 months
TEMPLATE — M&A or partnership activity expanding market coverage
TEMPLATE — Time lag between market trend emergence and vendor response (faster = higher score)

MKE.name: Marketing Execution & Brand
MKE.focus: TEMPLATE — quality, reach, and effectiveness of marketing programs in this specific market. How well does the vendor stand out in a competitive landscape? Maps to MQ criteria ATE-5 (Marketing Execution) and COV-2 (Marketing Strategy). Consider the key marketing channels for this market — research reports, conference presence, community, social media.
evidence_signals: TEMPLATE — Conference presence at key events for this market (e.g., RSA, Black Hat, market-specific summits)
TEMPLATE — Original research reports, threat intelligence publications, or thought leadership
TEMPLATE — Social media presence and SEO ranking on key category terms
TEMPLATE — Earned media coverage in relevant trade press

CXQ.name: Customer Experience Quality
CXQ.focus: TEMPLATE — quantitative and qualitative customer experience indicators for buyers in this specific market. Maps to MQ criterion ATE-6. Focus on onboarding experience, support quality, and post-sales success programs most relevant to this market. Example: time-to-value metrics for SaaS markets; service delivery quality for managed services markets.
evidence_signals: TEMPLATE — Gartner Peer Insights category rating and review count for this market
TEMPLATE — G2 or TrustRadius category position for this market
TEMPLATE — Published NRR (Net Revenue Retention) or DBNRR data
TEMPLATE — SLA documentation and support tier descriptions
TEMPLATE — Customer success program evidence (TAM, CSM, onboarding)

MKU.name: Market Understanding & Vision
MKU.focus: TEMPLATE — depth of understanding of buyer needs in this market, quality of product vision, and completeness of platform roadmap. Maps to MQ criteria COV-1 (Market Understanding) and COV-4 (Offering Strategy). What does a vendor who truly understands this market look like vs. one that is entering from an adjacent space without full understanding?
evidence_signals: TEMPLATE — CEO/CTO keynotes or blog posts articulating market direction
TEMPLATE — Public product roadmap or innovation announcements
TEMPLATE — Consumption-based or usage-based pricing models (evidence of understanding modern buyer expectations)
TEMPLATE — Patent filings or research investment evidence in core market technologies

VIG.name: Vertical & Geographic Strategy
VIG.focus: TEMPLATE — strategy for regulated verticals and geographic regions relevant to this market. Which verticals are most important for buyers in this market (financial services, healthcare, government, critical infrastructure)? Which geographic regions require specific compliance or data sovereignty considerations? Maps to MQ criteria COV-6 (Vertical/Industry Strategy) and COV-8 (Geographic Strategy).
evidence_signals: TEMPLATE — Regulatory compliance packs or certifications for relevant verticals (e.g., FedRAMP for US public sector, HIPAA for healthcare, PCI-DSS for financial services)
TEMPLATE — Regional availability and data residency options
TEMPLATE — Vertical-specific solution pages, case studies, or reference architectures
TEMPLATE — GovCloud, sovereign cloud, or regional cloud support where relevant

sub_pillars._note: Sub-pillars for MQ Gap schemas include scoring_guidance fields (unlike capability schemas) because MQ Gap criteria are harder to calibrate — what score-3 vs. score-5 means for 'Financial Viability' is less intuitive than a technical capability score. Include explicit scoring_guidance for each sub-pillar so different analysts reach consistent scores. Typical MQ Gap schema has 2-4 sub-pillars per pillar (14-28 total).

VIA-01.name: Revenue & Market Growth Trajectory
VIA-01.expanded_definition: TEMPLATE — annual revenue (total and market-segment-specific where available), year-over-year ARR or revenue growth, and trend over the last 3 years. For pure-play vendors, focus on segment ARR. For platform vendors, identify the specific business unit's contribution. Adjust the score-5 benchmark to match the scale of the target market.
what_to_verify_publicly: TEMPLATE — SEC filings or press releases showing segment revenue or ARR milestones
TEMPLATE — Funding announcements with valuation data (Crunchbase, press releases)
TEMPLATE — Analyst estimates of market share or revenue position in this segment
TEMPLATE — Cloud-security or market-specific headcount as a proxy for investment scale
search_terms: TEMPLATE — add market-specific qualifier (e.g., '[market name] revenue')

scoring_guidance.1: No revenue or ARR data publicly available
scoring_guidance.2: Revenue disclosed but flat or declining; no market-segment breakdown available
scoring_guidance.3: Positive growth documented; market segment identifiable; customer base growing
scoring_guidance.4: Strong documented growth (>30% YoY) with specific market-segment revenue; clear upward trajectory
scoring_guidance.5: TEMPLATE — define what market-leading revenue looks like for this specific market (e.g., '>$500M ARR' for CNAPP, '>$200M ARR' for a smaller market). Sustained high growth; transparent financials.

VIA-02.name: Profitability & Financial Health
VIA-02.expanded_definition: TEMPLATE — profitability indicators, cash position, burn rate for pure-play startups, and parent-company financial backing for platform vendors. This sub-pillar assesses whether the vendor will remain a viable long-term option for buyers making multi-year commitments.
what_to_verify_publicly: TEMPLATE — Profitability evidence (EBITDA, operating income from SEC filings)
TEMPLATE — Recent funding rounds indicating runway (ideally 2+ years)
TEMPLATE — Parent company financial backing and strategic commitment evidence
TEMPLATE — Rule of 40 score or free cash flow data where available

scoring_guidance.1: No financial health data available; high-risk funding stage with no recent rounds
scoring_guidance.2: Recent funding secured but high burn rate implied; or parent-company CNAPP is a minor underfunded initiative
scoring_guidance.3: Adequate runway (2+ years) for pure-plays; stable parent backing for platform vendors; breakeven trajectory
scoring_guidance.4: Profitable or near-profitable; strong cash position; documented commitment to sustained R&D in this market
scoring_guidance.5: Profitable with strong margins; investment-grade parent or unicorn-level valuation; substantial war chest for market investment

VIA-03.name: Customer Base & Retention
VIA-03.expanded_definition: TEMPLATE — published customer count for this market, enterprise logos, net retention rate, and customer base growth. Strong retention is a leading indicator of product-market fit and execution quality.
what_to_verify_publicly: TEMPLATE — Website customer logos page or published customer count
TEMPLATE — Market-specific case studies across multiple verticals
TEMPLATE — G2 / Gartner Peer Insights review counts as proxy for customer base size
TEMPLATE — SEC filings with customer metrics (NRR, DBNRR, customer count)

scoring_guidance.1: No customer count or logos published
scoring_guidance.2: A few customer logos or case studies; no count or retention data
scoring_guidance.3: Published customer count (100+); multiple case studies across sectors
scoring_guidance.4: Large customer base (500+); net retention data; expansion revenue documented; diverse verticals
scoring_guidance.5: TEMPLATE — define what a market-leading customer base looks like for this market size (e.g., 1000+ enterprise customers; published NRR >120%; multiple Fortune 100 logos)

SLE-01.name: Channel & Marketplace Presence
SLE-01.expanded_definition: TEMPLATE — marketplace listings, hyperscaler co-sell tiers (where applicable to this market), MSP/MSSP partner programs, and technology alliances with complementary vendors. Adjust focus based on dominant channel motions in this market — direct enterprise for some markets, heavy MSSP channel for services markets, hyperscaler marketplace for cloud markets.
what_to_verify_publicly: TEMPLATE — Marketplace listings with details (AWS, Azure, GCP for cloud; distributor listings for services)
TEMPLATE — Partner program tiers, named partners, and MSSP program documentation
TEMPLATE — Technology alliance pages with complementary vendor integrations
search_terms: TEMPLATE — marketplace term for this market

scoring_guidance.2: Minimal partner mentions; limited or undocumented channel
scoring_guidance.3: Documented partner program; some named partners; at least one relevant marketplace listing
scoring_guidance.4: Mature partner program (50+ partners); MSSP program with named providers; co-sell tier on major platforms
scoring_guidance.5: Best-in-class channel strategy for this market; 100+ partners; flagship MSSP/SI relationships; top co-sell tiers

SLE-02.name: Buying Experience & Trial Motion
SLE-02.expanded_definition: TEMPLATE — ease of evaluation for prospects: free trial availability, self-service onboarding, time-to-first-value, and product-led growth motion. The best-scoring vendors in modern markets (especially SaaS and cloud) enable prospects to evaluate the product without heavy sales friction. Adjust this sub-pillar to match the typical buying motion in this market.
what_to_verify_publicly: TEMPLATE — Free trial or POV program documentation
TEMPLATE — Self-service signup and onboarding flow
TEMPLATE — G2 reviews on buying and onboarding experience
TEMPLATE — Sales engineering job postings as proxy for pre-sales investment
search_terms: TEMPLATE — market-specific term (e.g., 'cloud connector' for CNAPP, 'free scan' for ASM)

scoring_guidance.1: Contact-us only; no trial or POV evidence
scoring_guidance.2: Demo request form only; no self-service evaluation path
scoring_guidance.3: Free trial or POV documented; onboarding guide available; sales team responsive
scoring_guidance.4: Self-service trial with rapid time-to-value; enterprise sales overlay for larger deals
scoring_guidance.5: Best-in-class PLG motion; sign-up and achieve first meaningful finding within 1 hour; multi-motion sales

MKR-01.name: Product Release Cadence & Velocity
MKR-01.expanded_definition: TEMPLATE — frequency and substance of product releases over the last 12-24 months. Fast-moving markets (AI security, cloud security) require higher release velocity to maintain competitiveness. Evaluate whether the vendor's release cadence keeps pace with market evolution.
what_to_verify_publicly: TEMPLATE — Release notes or changelog page (publicly accessible)
TEMPLATE — Blog posts announcing major new capabilities
TEMPLATE — What's New page or product update newsletters

scoring_guidance.1: No release history or changelog publicly available
scoring_guidance.2: Infrequent updates; quarterly+ releases with minor features
scoring_guidance.3: Monthly release cadence; meaningful feature additions; new capabilities documented
scoring_guidance.4: Bi-weekly releases; major capability additions; rapid coverage of market evolution
scoring_guidance.5: Continuous delivery; weekly releases; documented velocity metrics; same-week coverage of major market developments

MKR-02.name: Strategic Investment & M&A Activity
MKR-02.expanded_definition: TEMPLATE — evidence of strategic investment in this market through acquisitions, key technology partnerships, or major R&D investments. M&A activity can dramatically accelerate market position (see Palo Alto Prisma CNAPP acquisitions) or signal commitment to a market. Evaluate the strategic coherence and execution quality of any M&A.
what_to_verify_publicly: TEMPLATE — Acquisition announcements specific to this market
TEMPLATE — Technology partnership announcements expanding market capabilities
TEMPLATE — R&D investment announcements (headcount, lab openings, patent filings)

scoring_guidance.1: No M&A or strategic investment evidence in this market
scoring_guidance.2: Minor partnerships; no acquisitions; limited strategic investment signals
scoring_guidance.3: At least one meaningful strategic move (acquisition or major partnership) in the last 2 years
scoring_guidance.4: 2+ strategic acquisitions or partnerships that materially expand market capability; demonstrated integration success
scoring_guidance.5: Market-shaping M&A track record; multiple successful acquisitions integrated into coherent platform; defines market consolidation direction

MKE-01.name: Conference & Event Presence
MKE-01.expanded_definition: TEMPLATE — presence at key industry events relevant to this market. First-tier presence includes sponsoring or speaking at marquee events (RSA, Black Hat, market-specific summits). Second-tier includes presence at regional events. Score reflects both spend level and content quality — a gold sponsor with mediocre content scores lower than a thought-leadership speaker.
what_to_verify_publicly: TEMPLATE — Sponsorship tiers at key events for this market (website, event programs)
TEMPLATE — Speaking session recordings or abstracts at major events
TEMPLATE — Proprietary flagship event (e.g., annual user conference)
search_terms: TEMPLATE — key conference names for this market (e.g., RSA, KubeCon for cloud; Gartner Summit)

scoring_guidance.2: Minimal presence; exhibitor-only at one event
scoring_guidance.3: Sponsor and/or speaker at 1-2 major events; consistent annual presence
scoring_guidance.4: Prominent presence (title sponsor, keynote) at major events; multiple events annually
scoring_guidance.5: Defines conference presence in this market; hosts flagship user event; title sponsor at marquee shows; earned keynote positions

MKE-02.name: Content Marketing & Thought Leadership
MKE-02.expanded_definition: TEMPLATE — quality and reach of original research, threat intelligence, or thought leadership content specifically relevant to this market. High-quality, original content that shapes market conversation earns a score-5. Generic vendor blog posts with no original data earn a score-1 or score-2.
what_to_verify_publicly: TEMPLATE — Original research reports published in this market (annual threat reports, market analyses)
TEMPLATE — Blog post cadence and technical depth
TEMPLATE — SEO ranking on key category terms for this market
TEMPLATE — Social media presence and engagement (LinkedIn, X/Twitter)

scoring_guidance.1: No original content; corporate website only
scoring_guidance.2: Generic blog posts; no original research or data
scoring_guidance.3: Regular blog cadence with some original insights; 1 annual research report
scoring_guidance.4: Recognized thought leader in this market; multiple high-quality research publications; strong SEO presence
scoring_guidance.5: Defines thought leadership in this market; annual flagship research cited by competitors and analysts; community-building content

CXQ-01.name: Customer Satisfaction & Peer Review Ratings
CXQ-01.expanded_definition: TEMPLATE — quantitative satisfaction metrics from peer review platforms relevant to this market. Look for market-specific categories on Gartner Peer Insights and G2. Review count matters as well as rating — a 4.9/5 from 10 reviews is less meaningful than a 4.6/5 from 500 reviews.
what_to_verify_publicly: TEMPLATE — Gartner Peer Insights category and rating for this market
TEMPLATE — G2 category position and overall rating for this market
TEMPLATE — TrustRadius or PeerSpot data if available for this market
TEMPLATE — Customer testimonials citing specific value delivered
search_terms: TEMPLATE — add market-specific review platform terms

scoring_guidance.2: Minimal reviews (<20); below-average rating; or no market-specific category
scoring_guidance.3: Adequate review base (50+); average or above-average rating (4.0+); market-specific category present
scoring_guidance.4: Strong review base (200+); high rating (4.4+); consistent positive themes across reviews
scoring_guidance.5: Market-leading peer review position; 500+ reviews; category leader on major platforms; 4.6+ rating; Gartner Peer Insights 'Voice of the Customer' recognition

CXQ-02.name: Support Quality & Customer Success
CXQ-02.expanded_definition: TEMPLATE — post-sales support quality, customer success program maturity, and documented time-to-value. For services markets, this includes service delivery quality. For product markets, this includes implementation support and onboarding speed.
what_to_verify_publicly: TEMPLATE — SLA documentation (response times, uptime guarantees)
TEMPLATE — Customer success program evidence (dedicated TAM, CSM programs, named accounts)
TEMPLATE — Onboarding or implementation documentation
TEMPLATE — Reviews mentioning support quality specifically

scoring_guidance.1: No SLA or support documentation; no customer success evidence
scoring_guidance.2: Basic support documentation; no dedicated customer success motion
scoring_guidance.3: Documented SLA tiers; customer success program described; positive support reviews
scoring_guidance.4: Named TAM/CSM programs for enterprise accounts; strong SLA tiers; documented fast time-to-value
scoring_guidance.5: Best-in-class support in this market; proactive customer success; industry-leading SLA; documented retention programs

MKU-01.name: Market Vision & Innovation Roadmap
MKU-01.expanded_definition: TEMPLATE — clarity and ambition of market vision, public roadmap communications, and alignment between stated direction and actual execution. Vendors who articulate where the market is going (and deliver on it) score higher. Vendors who are reactive or whose roadmap is opaque score lower.
what_to_verify_publicly: TEMPLATE — CEO/CTO public statements on market direction (keynotes, interviews)
TEMPLATE — Public roadmap page or roadmap blog posts
TEMPLATE — Analyst briefing summaries or third-party coverage of vendor vision
TEMPLATE — Patent filings in core market technology areas

scoring_guidance.1: No vision or roadmap information publicly available
scoring_guidance.2: Vague vision; no specific roadmap commitments; reactive positioning
scoring_guidance.3: Documented vision with some roadmap details; reasonable alignment to market trends
scoring_guidance.4: Compelling market vision; specific roadmap with milestone tracking; ahead of market curve on at least one dimension
scoring_guidance.5: Market-shaping vision; defined the conversation in this market; roadmap demonstrates deep buyer understanding; first-mover on emerging trends

VIG-01.name: Vertical Industry Strategy
VIG-01.expanded_definition: TEMPLATE — dedicated vertical solutions, compliance packs, or reference architectures for regulated industries most important to this market. Identify the top 2-3 verticals for this market and evaluate the depth of vertical-specific investment.
what_to_verify_publicly: TEMPLATE — Vertical solution pages (financial services, healthcare, government, critical infrastructure)
TEMPLATE — Compliance certifications most relevant to verticals in this market
TEMPLATE — Vertical-specific case studies or reference architectures
TEMPLATE — Vertical-specific sales or customer success teams

scoring_guidance.1: No vertical-specific content, certifications, or solutions
scoring_guidance.2: Generic compliance mentions; no vertical-specific depth or dedicated resources
scoring_guidance.3: 1-2 key verticals addressed with specific solutions or case studies
scoring_guidance.4: 3+ verticals with dedicated resources; relevant compliance certifications documented; vertical-specific marketing
scoring_guidance.5: Comprehensive vertical strategy; leading certifications (FedRAMP, IL5 where relevant); multiple regulated verticals with dedicated teams and named reference customers

VIG-02.name: Geographic Coverage & Data Sovereignty
VIG-02.expanded_definition: TEMPLATE — geographic availability, data residency options, and support for regional regulatory requirements relevant to buyers in this market. For globally-deployed products, evaluate breadth of regional availability. For data-sensitive markets, evaluate the depth of data residency and sovereignty options.
what_to_verify_publicly: TEMPLATE — Regional availability pages or documentation
TEMPLATE — Data residency documentation (where data is stored, processed, and retained)
TEMPLATE — Sovereign cloud or GovCloud support where relevant to this market
TEMPLATE — Regional partner or support infrastructure evidence

scoring_guidance.1: Single-region only; no data residency options
scoring_guidance.3: 3 major regions (Americas, EMEA, APAC); basic data residency options
scoring_guidance.4: 4+ regions; documented data residency by region; sovereign or GovCloud options for key markets
scoring_guidance.5: Global presence; comprehensive data residency options for all major regulatory regimes; dedicated sovereign cloud or GovCloud with named customers; 20+ country coverage
